meta.title: Is It Tuesday?
meta.sub: in which a happy man comes to the city
meta.logline: Haru leaves his grandmother's lighthouse for Tokyo, fails three job interviews, crashes into an heiress on a zebra crossing, faints, and ends up with her phone.

shots.text: On a small island with one lighthouse, one goat, and three thousand donated books, lived a very happy man.
Ferry's here. Have you got everything?
One suitcase, one cactus, one library card. And my umbrella. Probably.
Haru. The city is very big, and very beautiful in places. Try not to faint at it.
I'll try, Grandma. I'll only look at the ugly parts.
And phone me on Sundays.
Is it Sunday today?
It's Tuesday, you silly boy. Go.
And this is your room! Six tatami, one window, no furniture, very cheap.
It has a window! A whole window!
Most rooms do, young man.
Not in a lighthouse. In a lighthouse the window has a very big lamp in it and you're not allowed to touch it.
A lighthouse? You grew up in a lighthouse? Hm. I'm writing that down.
Mister Kobayashi writes everything down. He also reads your mail.
By accident! It only happens by accident!
Every day. By accident.
Hello! I'm Haru. This is Lev. He's a cactus.
Why does your cactus have a face?
Why does yours not?
Huh.
Rent is due on the first. Do you have a job, Mister Mishima?
Not yet. I'll get one tomorrow. Today I'm going to look out of the window.
Bet you won't get one.
Bet I will! What are we betting?
Your cactus.
Never mind. Let's bet candy.
Nobody comes up here but me and the tomatoes. You can see the whole city.
Oh. Oh no. It's very beautiful. Hold my cactus.
Are you... fainting? At Tokyo?
Almost. I've got it now. It helps if I count the ugly buildings.
So you really faint at beautiful things. Is that a medical condition?
The doctor called it a very sensitive nervous system. Grandma calls it being paid attention to by the world.
When I was little I fainted so often they sent me to the island. Grandma kept the lighthouse. The library sent us their old books, three thousand of them, and I read every one. Twice.
Three thousand books, and you still came to Tokyo with no job?
None of the books were about jobs. They were mostly about people being kind to each other, and then not.
Let me tell you something about this city, Mister Mishima. A man who always tells the truth here is either a saint or an idiot.
Which one am I?
Ask me again on the first of the month.
Why do you want to work at Sunrise Insurance?
I don't, really. But Mister Kobayashi says rent is due on the first.
What is your greatest weakness?
I faint at beautiful things. Sunsets, mostly. Once a very handsome goat.
Where do you see yourself in five years?
Alive, I hope! Is that too ambitious?
Forty-one interviews! That's a lot of very nice people who don't want me.
Haru Mishima. No job. No girlfriend, ever. No money. And somehow, the happiest man in Tokyo.
Grandma! Is it Sunday?
No, it's Tuesday. I worried. Did you faint?
Only a little, on a roof. And I went to three interviews. Everybody was very polite and nobody wanted me.
Did you tell them the truth again?
I tried to tell them a lie once, but it came out as the truth halfway through.
Then don't change, Haru. The right door will open for the wrong reasons. It usually does.
Give Professor a carrot from me.
He's eating my slipper. I'll tell him you said hello.
Fifty-two floors up, in a penthouse with forty-two staff and zero parents, lived Nana Kurosaki.
Nana! You just hit two million followers!
Two million! That's like, a whole city of people who love you!
Darling, two million people love my shoes. It's different.
Did your dad call for your birthday?
He sent a car. A whole car, with a bow on it. He's very consistent. He sends a car instead of a phone call every year.
You have nine cars, Nana.
Ten. I'm saving up for a parking garage.
Party's at your place Friday, right? Your birthday. Twenty-five. Ancient.
Say it louder, Taku. The doorman didn't hear.
Selfie! Everybody, selfie!
Good evening, ladies. Gentleman. Nana, a word.
Mister Togashi. My guardian. My accountant. My weather forecast. What's the forecast?
At your party on Friday, the board would like you to consider a proposal.
A proposal. Like a business proposal?
Like a marriage proposal. From Mister Ryuji Gozen. He is very rich and very interested.
Is he interested in me, or in the hotel?
Is there a difference, my dear?
Tell the board I'm exclusive. Good night, Mister Togashi.
Two million followers. Four best friends. Forty-two staff. And I can't think of one person to call.
Tomorrow I'll buy something enormous. That always helps. For about an hour.
Hey! Watch where you're walking! Do you have any idea who I am?
No. Do you?
Excuse me?
Oh no.
Oh no, what?
You're beautiful.
Did he just... faint? On a zebra crossing?
Wow. I've had men fall for me, but never literally.
She stepped over him and went to buy something enormous. She did not notice that her phone had landed in his cardigan pocket.

shots.shot: insert:phone:47 missed calls\nMIKA: where r u lol

shots.text: That's Nana Kurosaki's phone! The Nana Kurosaki! You stole the most famous phone in Tokyo!
I didn't steal it. It fell into my pocket while I was unconscious.
Nana Kurosaki. Heiress of Hotel Kurosaki. Mother gone, father in Singapore, raised by the staff. Engaged, they say, to a crypto king.
How do you know all that?
Magazines. And her doorman's mail. By accident.
She looked very tired. Like someone who'd been crying at three in the morning.
She looked rich, Haru.
You can be both. I'll take it back to her tomorrow.
To the Hotel Kurosaki? Dressed like that? They'll throw you out.
Then I'll have been thrown out of a very nice hotel. That's a new experience!
Deliveries are round the back, sir.
I'm not a delivery. Well, I'm delivering a phone. So maybe I am a delivery.
Miss Kurosaki does not receive visitors in cardigans.
Let him up, Kenji. I want to see what a man who faints at women looks like when he's conscious.
Here's your phone. Forty-seven missed calls. And a message that says, where are you, L-O-L.
Thank you. What do you want? Money? A selfie? A job?
Oh, no. I just wanted to give it back. And to ask if you're all right.
If I'm... all right?
Yesterday you looked like you hadn't slept. Like you'd been awake at three in the morning with nobody to call.
Who told you that?
Your face did. Faces are very honest. It's the mouths that tell lies.
Nana! Who's the guy in the grandpa cardigan?
He looks like a lost sheep!
He looks like an idiot.
I probably am! My grandma says so too, but nicely.
You know what? You're hired. My personal assistant. For one week.
A job? I have a job! Kenta owes me candy!
Rules. One: you carry my bags. Two: you never fall in love with me. Three: you never faint in public. It's embarrassing.
One, yes. Three, I'll do my best. Two, I can't promise. I haven't decided yet.
You haven't... decided?
It seems like a big decision. I'll let you know on Friday.
He's perfect. Nana, he's perfect. I'll give him three days before he cries.
Don't get excited. It's a joke for my friends. You're the joke.
That's all right. I like jokes. Is it Tuesday?
It's Wednesday, idiot.
Oh, good. I like Wednesdays.

shots.shot: insert:letter:Good night!\nIs it Thursday tomorrow?\n- Haru (your assistant)
shots.text: Good night! Is it Thursday tomorrow? From Haru, your assistant.
It's Thursday tomorrow, idiot.
I'm not going to answer him. I'm absolutely not going to answer him.
She answered him. And for the first time in a long time, at three in the morning, Nana Kurosaki fell asleep.
Next time on Beautiful Idiot: my first day as an assistant! I carry bags, I ride a bus, and I buy a very good umbrella. The Hundred Yen Umbrella. Is it raining?
